extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and docketing staff preparing or prosecuting U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements governing who may apply for a U.S. patent, how inventorship and applicant status are established or corrected, and the formal/content/formatting requisites of patent (nonprovisional and provisional) applications filed with the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney revocation and Customer Number treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney to the patent practitioners associated with a Customer Number will be treated as a request to revoke any powers of attorney previously given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fewer than all applicants (or assignees/owners in certain proceedings) may revoke a power of attorney only upon a showing of sufficient cause and payment of the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(f). A patent practitioner will be notified of the revocation. When power of attorney is given to practitioners associated with a Customer Number, practitioners so appointed will be notified when the power of attorney to all practitioners associated with that Customer Number is revoked. The notice of revocation will be mailed to the correspondence address for the application (§ 1.33). An assignment does not of itself operate as a revocation of a prior power of attorney, but the assignee of the entire interest may revoke previous powers and give another power as provided in § 1.32(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of registered patent attorney/agent
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent attorney or patent agent given a power of attorney may withdraw as attorney or agent of record upon application to and approval by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant or patent owner will be notified of the withdrawal. If power of attorney is given to practitioners associated with a Customer Number, a request to delete all practitioners may not be granted if an Office action is outstanding and insufficient time remains for the applicant to file a reply. See § 41.5 for withdrawal during PTAB proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include inventor name(s) (§ 1.41(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include, or be amended to include, the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable to applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or 363 on or after Sept. 16, 2012 (editor note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for nonprovisional applications (§ 1.41(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship is the inventor(s) set forth in the application data sheet (§ 1.76) filed before or concurrently with the inventor's oath or declaration; if no ADS filed before/concurrently, inventorship is as set forth in the inventor's oath/declaration, except as provided by §§ 1.53(d)(4) and 1.63(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an ADS or the inventor's oath/declaration is filed, any correction of inventorship must be pursuant to § 1.48. If neither an ADS nor oath/declaration is filed during pendency, inventorship is as set forth in application papers filed pursuant to § 1.53(b), unless the applicant files a paper (with processing fee § 1.17(i)) supplying the inventor name(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for provisional applications (§ 1.41(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of a provisional application is the inventor(s) set forth in the cover sheet prescribed by § 1.51(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the prescribed cover sheet is filed, any correction of inventorship must be pursuant to § 1.48. If the cover sheet is not filed during pendency, inventorship is as set forth in application papers filed pursuant to § 1.53(c), unless applicant files a paper with the processing fee (§ 1.17(q)) supplying the inventor name(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for international (national stage) applications (§ 1.41(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of an international application entering the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 is the inventor(s) set forth in the ADS (§ 1.76) filed with the initial submission under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the initial submission lacks an ADS, inventorship is as set forth in the international application, including any change effected under PCT Rule 92bis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for international design applications (§ 1.41(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of an international design application designating the United States is the creator(s) set forth in the publication of the international registration under Hague Agreement Article 10(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any correction of inventorship must be pursuant to § 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must be actual inventor(s) (pre-AIA § 1.41 (pre-AIA) / § 1.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is applied for in the name(s) of the actual inventor(s); 'applicant' refers to the inventor(s) or to a person applying in place of the inventor under §§ 1.42, 1.43 or 1.47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisional applications, inventorship is that set forth in the oath/declaration (§ 1.63) or application papers (§ 1.53(b)). For provisional applications, inventorship is as set forth in the cover sheet (§ 1.51(c)(1)) or application papers (§ 1.53(c)). Name, residence (and citizenship pre-AIA) of each believed actual inventor should be provided when papers under § 1.53(b)/(c) are filed if no oath/cover sheet filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'applicant' and who may apply (§ 1.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'applicant' refers to the inventor or all joint inventors, or to the person applying for a patent as provided in §§ 1.43, 1.45, or 1.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a person applies under § 1.46 (assignee/obligated assignee/sufficient proprietary interest), 'applicant' refers to that person, not the inventor. Any person having authority may deliver an application and fees to the Office for the applicant, but oaths/declarations, correspondence addresses, and signed amendments must comply with §§ 1.63/1.64 and § 1.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by legal representative of deceased/incapacitated inventor (§§ 1.43 / pre-AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is deceased or under legal incapacity, the legal representative (executor, administrator, guardian, conservator, etc.) may make the application and execute the necessary oath/declaration or substitute statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventor dies between filing and grant, letters patent may be issued to the legal representative upon proper intervention. See § 1.64 for substitute statement execution by a legal representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors must apply jointly and make oath/declaration (§ 1.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint inventors must apply for a patent jointly, and each must make an inventor's oath or declaration as required by § 1.63, except as provided in § 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joint inventor refuses to join or cannot be found after diligent effort, the other joint inventor(s) may make the application on behalf of themselves and the omitted inventor, accompanied by a petition and substitute statement as discussed in § 1.64.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted joint application even without equal contributions (§ 1.45(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors may apply jointly even though they did not physically work together or at the same time, each did not make the same type or amount of contribution, or each did not contribute to the subject matter of every claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint application is appropriate where each named inventor made a contribution to at least one claim (nonprovisional) or to the subject matter disclosed (provisional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution requirement for named inventors (§ 1.45(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple inventors are named in a nonprovisional application, each named inventor must have made a contribution, individually or jointly, to the subject matter of at least one claim; for provisional applications, each named inventor must have made a contribution to the subject matter disclosed in the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If satisfied, the application will be considered a joint application under 35 U.S.C. 116.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by assignee or party with proprietary interest (§ 1.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign the invention, or a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter, may make an application for patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a person applies under 35 U.S.C. 111, the application must contain an ADS (§ 1.76) specifying the assignee or person in the applicant information section. For international-stage or international design applications, the assignee/sufficient-interest person must have been identified earlier. Documentary evidence of ownership (e.g., assignment, employment agreement) should be recorded (part 3) no later than date issue fee is paid. A person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest must submit a petition including fee § 1.17(g), a showing of sufficient proprietary interest, and a statement that making the application by that person is appropriate to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or update of applicant name (§ 1.46(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or update the name of the applicant must include an application data sheet (§ 1.76) specifying the correct or updated applicant name in the applicant information section and comply with recording provisions (e.g., §§ 3.71 and 3.73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change in applicant after an original applicant has been specified must include an ADS and comply with §§ 3.71 and 3.73.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration requirement despite assignment (§ 1.46(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if all or part of the interest in the invention or patent is assigned or obligated to be assigned, an oath or declaration must be executed by the actual inventor or each actual joint inventor, except as provided in § 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.64 for execution of a substitute statement by an assignee or person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship procedures and fees (§ 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to correct or change inventorship after inventorship is established must include an ADS (§ 1.76) identifying each inventor by legal name and the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An oath/declaration (§ 1.63) or substitute statement (§ 1.64) is required for any actual inventor who has not executed one. If the request is filed after an Office action on the merits has been given/mailed, it must also be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(d), unless the request is solely due to cancellation of claims. For provisional applications, once the cover sheet is filed, requests to correct inventorship must include a signed request by a party set forth in § 1.33(b) identifying each inventor, and include the processing fee (§ 1.17(q)). The Office may require additional information. Correction/updating of inventor name or order requires an ADS per § 1.76 and fee § 1.17(i). This section does not apply to reissue applications; see §§ 1.171 and 1.175. Correction in a patent is addressed at § 1.324. Correction in interferences or contested PTAB cases must be motions under part 41/42 rules (e.g., § 41.121(a)(2) or § 42.22) and comply with paragraph (a) of § 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application contents (nonprovisional) (§ 1.51(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application filed under § 1.53(b) or § 1.53(d) comprises: (1) a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 including a claim or claims (see §§ 1.71–1.77); (2) the inventor's oath or declaration (see §§ 1.63 and 1.64); (3) drawings, when necessary (see §§ 1.81–1.85); and (4) the prescribed filing fee, search fee, examination fee, and application size fee (see § 1.16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to file an information disclosure statement in nonprovisional applications (§§ 1.97 and 1.98); no IDS may be filed in a provisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete provisional application contents (§ 1.51(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete provisional application filed under § 1.53(c) comprises: (1) a cover sheet identifying that it is a provisional and listing inventor name(s), residence, title of the invention, attorney/agent name and registration number (if applicable), docket number (if applicable), correspondence address, and U.S. Government agency & contract number (if applicable); (2) a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a); (3) drawings when necessary; and (4) the prescribed filing fee and application size fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.51(c)(1) for exact cover sheet fields; provisional applications may not include an information disclosure statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper physical and layout requirements (§ 1.52(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers to become part of the permanent USPTO records (other than drawings) submitted on paper/facsimile must be on sheets that are the same size, not permanently bound, and: flexible, strong, smooth, non-shiny, durable, white; be either DIN A4 (21.0 x 29.7 cm) or 8.5 x 11 inches (21.6 x 27.9 cm) with top margin ≥2.0 cm (3/4 in), left margin ≥2.5 cm (1 in), right and bottom margins ≥2.0 cm (3/4 in); written on only one side in portrait orientation; plainly and legibly typewritten or machine printed in permanent dark ink (or equivalent); and presented with sufficient clarity and contrast to permit reproduction by photographic/electrostatic/photo-offset/microfilming and electronic capture/optical character recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These paper provisions do not apply to pre-printed Office forms or to paper copies of patents submitted in double-column format as the specification in a reissue application or reexamination request. See § 1.58 for chemical/mathematical formulae/tables and § 1.84 for drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in submitted sheets (§ 1.52(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers submitted on paper or by facsimile transmission that will become part of the permanent records should have no holes in the sheets as submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission formatting requirement (§ 1.52(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted electronically to the Office must be formatted and transmitted in compliance with the USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application language requirement (§ 1.52(b)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application and any amendments or corrections must comply with paper/format requirements and be in the English language or be accompanied by a translation into English and a statement that the translation is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification (including abstract and claims) and amendments must have lines 1.5 or double spaced, use a nonscript font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier, preferably font size 12), capital letters should be at least 0.3175 cm (0.125 in) high but may be no smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 in) (e.g., font size 6), and the text should be a single column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims and abstract placement and page numbering (§ 1.52(b)(3)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim(s) must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page. The abstract must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page or be submitted as the first page of the patent in certain proceedings. Pages of the specification (including claims and abstract) must be numbered consecutively starting with 1, centrally located above or preferably below the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules have exceptions for reissue and reexamination/supplemental examination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph numbering in specification (§ 1.52(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs of the specification (other than claims or abstract) may be numbered at filing and should be individually and consecutively numbered using Arabic numerals, at least four numerals enclosed in square brackets (e.g., [0001]) including leading zeros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph numbers and enclosing brackets should appear to the right of the left margin as the first item in each paragraph before the first word, and should be highlighted in bold. (Text references a required gap equivalent to ... ; formatting guidance truncated in chunk.)
